messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool-queue-length > 2500 for 6m, enqueue_rate spike detected. Auto-remediation (scale) attempted and failed (reason: scaler-lock).

alex: saw this, queue growing in prod-inference. 5xx spike, latency climbing to ~2.8s P95. tagging oncall.

mariana: paging. i'm on it. oncall window. grabbing logs now.

alex: baseline: we should be able to add 3 nodes but autoscaler is stuck in "AcquireLock" for ~4m. looks like a leader election / lock contention with the k8s-cluster-autoscaler.

opsbot: Autoscaler event: Failed to acquire lock: ResourceBusyError (holder: autoscaler-standby). Attempted 6 times.

mariana: copying recent controller logs.

mariana: ```
I0315 03:05:12.345 scaler.go:216] attempting scale up: want 3, max 10
E0315 03:05:16.117 leader_election.go:98] failed to acquire lease: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = context deadline exceeded
E0315 03:05:18.889 scaler.go:430] unable to scale: lock not acquired, backing off
```

jordan: any IAM errors in the provisioner? last time this looked like permission rejections from the profile.

eng-runtime: checking cloud provider logs... there's a flurry of API 429s to EC2 RunInstances and AttachRole calls around the same time. likely hitting a rate limit combined with rapid requests.

sam: customers seeing timeouts on /v1/generate, rate of error responses ~8% for GPU-backed routes. non-GPU fallback capacity healthy but can't match throughput -> queue backpressure.

alex: quick mitigation options: 1) manually increase ASG desired count for gpu-pool-02, 2) temporarily enable preemptible fallback routing to small-quantized model, 3) force release autoscaler lock by restarting deployment. pros/cons?

mariana: prefer manual ASG bump first (least risky). will coordinate with infra to avoid weird launchtemplate drift. tagging @sre_lead for approval.

sre_lead: +1 to manual bump. also want logging snapshot and to avoid taint mismatches. if ASG fails, we may restart autoscaler after increasing provider API backoff.

opsbot: Incident severity: P2 -> escalate to P1 if customer 5xx > 10% sustained. Current customer impact limited to 3 large tenants with degraded latency.

mariana: @infra-team please run: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-02 --desired-capacity 8 --honor-cooldown`

eng-runtime: note: launch template version v2 is different from v3 that other pools use. confirm AMI and instance profile.

jordan: checking IAM: instance-profile/gpu-launch-profile has valid AttachRole policy but there were 429s earlier; shouldn't be permanent.

mariana: ASG update in progress, console shows new instances provisioning (3 of 3 requested). provisioning stuck on instance profile association for one instance. quick check logs: `AttachInstanceProfile` returned 500 for i-0abcde.

alex: if instance profile attach is flaky, we can spin a node from gpu-fallback-pool which already has profile attached. fallback pool has 2 spare capacity.

mariana: doing that now: `aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-fallback-pool --desired-capacity 2 --honor-cooldown`

eng-runtime: provider API error rate is settling after backoff; new fallback nodes are joining. kube nodes show `Ready` for 2 new nodes.

sam: traffic routing updated: temporarily shift 40% of new requests to CPU-quantized instance group and 60% to GPU as they come online. error rate dropped to 3%.

mariana: to unblock autoscaler permanently, i'm going to restart the autoscaler controller to clear the lock and let it re-evaluate. scheduling now.

mariana: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/cluster-autoscaler`

opsbot: Action logged by mariana at 03:14 UTC.

eng-runtime: autoscaler restarted, successfully acquired lease. immediately scaled to desired target and recognized the 2 new fallback nodes; additional scale up to 3 GPU nodes initiated.

jordan: after restart we see no more leader election errors. cloud provider 429s reduced after backoff; monitoring shows RunInstances latency back to normal.

sam: customer-facing update: sent message to three affected tenants: temporary degraded throughput during 03:03-03:20 UTC. no data loss, mitigation in place.

mariana: final checks: drained 1 misbehaving instance, cleared a stale taint that prevented pod scheduling (`node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule`) that was accidentally left by previous eviction job.

alex: root cause analysis hypothesis: brief surge triggered concurrent scale requests -> provider API rate limits + lock contention in autoscaler (leader election timeouts) -> scale up attempts failed -> queue built up. contributing: mixed launch template versions and a stale taint leftover from a prior eviction flow increased scheduling friction.

eng-runtime: next steps: 1) increase provider backoff settings for autoscaler, 2) add ephemeral jitter to scale attempts to reduce simultaneous API calls, 3) audit and standardize launch template versions across gpu pools, 4) add health check to clear stale taints automatically after evictions.

mariana: I've handed this to daytime SRE for follow-up. leaving runbook pointers and logs in the incident doc. :white_check_mark:

sre_lead: closing pager for now. any objections?

jordan: none from infra. good catch.

sam: closing customer comms after we verify 1h of stable 5xx < 0.5%.

incident-bot: Incident note: mitigated, monitoring.
